verses.text: Family, here’s the Good News I preached to you—the message you received and are standing on.
That’s the message saving you, if you hold firmly to what I preached. Otherwise, your faith may have been for nothing.
First things first: I passed on what I also received—that Christ died for our sins, just as the Scriptures said;
he was buried, and on the third day he was raised, just as the Scriptures said;
then he appeared to Cephas, and after that to the twelve.
After that he appeared to more than five hundred believers at once. Most are still alive, though some have died.
Then he appeared to James, and after that to all the apostles.
Last of all, like someone born way too late, he appeared to me too.
I’m the least of the apostles. I don’t even deserve to be called one, because I persecuted God’s church.
But God’s grace made me who I am. His grace wasn’t wasted: I worked harder than all of them—though really, it was God’s grace working with me.
So whether it was me or the others, this is what we preach, and this is what you believed.
Now if we preach that Christ was raised from the dead, how can some of you say there’s no resurrection of the dead?
If the dead aren’t raised, then Christ wasn’t raised either.
And if Christ wasn’t raised, our preaching is empty and your faith is empty too.
Then we’d also be lying witnesses about God, because we testified that he raised Christ—something he couldn’t have done if the dead aren’t raised.
If the dead aren’t raised, then Christ wasn’t raised.
And if Christ wasn’t raised, your faith is useless and you’re still stuck in your sins.
Then the believers who died trusting Christ are gone for good.
If our hope in Christ is only for this life, we’re the most pitiful people around.
But here’s the truth: Christ has been raised from the dead! He’s the firstfruits of those who have died. 🌅
Death came through a human being, and resurrection from the dead also came through a human being.
Just as everyone dies in Adam, everyone will be made alive in Christ.
But there’s an order: Christ is the firstfruits; then, when he comes, those who belong to him.
After that comes the end, when Christ hands the Kingdom over to God the Father, after abolishing every rule, authority, and power.
He must reign until he has put every enemy under his feet.
The last enemy to be abolished is death.
Scripture says, “He put everything under his feet.” When it says “everything,” that obviously doesn’t include the One who put everything under Christ.
When everything has been put under Christ, then the Son himself will also be subject to the One who put everything under him, so God may be everything to everyone.
Otherwise, what are people doing who get baptized for the dead? If the dead aren’t raised at all, why get baptized for them?
And why are we putting our lives on the line every hour?
Family, I face death every day. I swear that’s true, just as surely as I’m proud of you in Christ Jesus our Lord.
If I fought wild beasts in Ephesus just for human reasons, what did I gain? If the dead aren’t raised, “let’s eat and drink, because tomorrow we die.”
Don’t get fooled: “Bad company ruins good character.”
Wake up and live right—stop sinning! Some of you don’t know God at all, and you should be embarrassed.
But someone will ask, “How are the dead raised? What kind of body will they have?”
Come on, think about it: what you plant doesn’t come to life unless it dies first.
What you plant isn’t the full-grown plant; it’s just a bare seed, maybe wheat or something else.
But God gives it the body he chooses, and each kind of seed gets its own body.
Not all flesh is the same: humans have one kind, animals another, birds another, and fish another.
There are heavenly bodies and earthly bodies, and their glory isn’t the same.
The sun has its own glory, the moon another, and the stars another. Even one star differs from another in glory.
It’s like that with the resurrection of the dead: the body is planted perishable, but raised imperishable.
It’s planted in dishonor, raised in glory; planted in weakness, raised in power.
It’s planted as a natural body and raised as a spiritual body. There’s a natural body, and there’s a spiritual body too.
Scripture says, “The first man, Adam, became a living being.” The last Adam became a life-giving Spirit.
But the spiritual didn’t come first. The natural came first, then the spiritual.
The first man came from the earth, made from dust; the second man came from heaven.
Those made from dust are like the one made from dust, and those from heaven are like the one from heaven.
Just as we’ve carried the image of the man made from dust, let’s also carry the image of the man from heaven.
Here’s what I mean, family: flesh and blood can’t inherit God’s Kingdom, and what decays can’t inherit what never decays.
Listen, I’m telling you a mystery: not all of us will die, but all of us will be changed—
in an instant, in the blink of an eye, at the last trumpet. The trumpet will sound, the dead will be raised imperishable, and we’ll be changed.
This perishable body has to put on what can’t decay, and this mortal body has to put on immortality.
When that happens, Scripture’s words will come true: “Death has been swallowed up in victory.”
“Death, where’s your sting? Grave, where’s your victory?”
Death’s sting is sin, and sin gets its power from the Law.
But thanks be to God! He gives us the victory through our Lord Jesus Christ. 🙌
So, my dear family, stand firm and don’t budge. Keep giving yourselves fully to the Lord’s work, because you know your work for the Lord isn’t wasted.
